questions.stem: The RESERVE BANK OF INDIA (RBI) was established on:

options.option_text: 1 APRIL 1935 — under the RBI Act 1934, based on recommendations of the HILTON YOUNG COMMISSION (1926); nationalised 1 Jan 1949

questions.explanation: RESERVE BANK OF INDIA (RBI) — India's CENTRAL BANK. KEY DATES: (1) 1926 — HILTON YOUNG COMMISSION (Royal Commission on Indian Currency + Finance) recommended separate central bank. (2) 1934 — RESERVE BANK OF INDIA ACT enacted. (3) 1 APRIL 1935 — RBI commenced operations (Calcutta, later Bombay in 1937). (4) 1 JANUARY 1949 — RBI NATIONALISED (earlier a privately-owned shareholders' bank). (5) 1949 — BANKING REGULATION ACT. HEADQUARTERS: MUMBAI (previously Calcutta). GOVERNOR: constitutional head, appointed by Central Government. First Governor: SIR OSBORNE SMITH (1935-37, Australian). First Indian Governor: C.D. DESHMUKH (1943-49). Other notable Governors: Manmohan Singh (1982-85), Y.V. Reddy (2003-08), Raghuram Rajan (2013-16), Urjit Patel (2016-18), Shaktikanta Das (2018-24), SANJAY MALHOTRA (current from Dec 2024). FUNCTIONS: (a) ISSUING currency; (b) BANKER to Government + commercial banks; (c) Regulator + supervisor of banks; (d) CONTROLLER of money supply (monetary policy); (e) Manager of exchange rate + forex reserves; (f) Developmental role. Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) — 6 members (3 RBI + 3 external), decides repo rate since 2016.

questions.stem: The FIRST modern BANK established in India was:

options.option_text: BANK OF HINDUSTAN (1770, Calcutta) — failed by 1832; Bank of Bengal (1806) later merged into SBI (1955)

questions.explanation: FIRST BANK of INDIA — BANK OF HINDUSTAN, est. 1770 in CALCUTTA by British merchants Alexander + Co.; failed by 1832. CHRONOLOGY: (1) 1770 — Bank of Hindustan. (2) 1786 — General Bank of India. (3) 1806 — BANK OF CALCUTTA (later BANK OF BENGAL in 1809). (4) 1840 — BANK OF BOMBAY. (5) 1843 — BANK OF MADRAS. The 3 Presidency banks merged in 1921 as IMPERIAL BANK OF INDIA; NATIONALISED + renamed STATE BANK OF INDIA (SBI) on 1 JULY 1955 by SBI Act 1955 (SBI's foundation day). FIRST INDIAN-OWNED bank: OUDH COMMERCIAL BANK (Faizabad, 1881 — failed 1958). FIRST INDIAN-owned bank still operating: PUNJAB NATIONAL BANK (PNB, Lahore/Delhi, 1894, founded by Lala Lajpat Rai, Dyal Singh Majithia + others — first bank 'managed + owned entirely by Indians with Indian capital'). Later Nationalisation rounds: 1969 (14 banks), 1980 (6 more). Since 2017 — wave of MERGERS reduced public-sector banks to 12: SBI absorbed associates + BMB; Vijaya+Dena into BoB; PNB+OBC+UBI; Canara+Syndicate; Union+Andhra+Corporation; Indian+Allahabad (all April 2020).

questions.stem: The REPO RATE is the rate at which:

options.option_text: RBI LENDS short-term funds to commercial banks against government securities (repurchase agreement)

questions.explanation: REPO RATE (REPURCHASE RATE) — rate at which RBI LENDS short-term funds to commercial BANKS against pledged government securities with agreement to repurchase. BENCHMARK POLICY RATE set by the MONETARY POLICY COMMITTEE (MPC), 6 members (3 RBI + 3 external), since 2016 amendment to RBI Act. Meets BI-MONTHLY. repo ↑ → banks' cost ↑ → lending rates ↑ → dampens inflation. repo ↓ → stimulates growth. CURRENT (Apr 2026): ~6.50%. RELATED RATES: (1) REVERSE REPO RATE — rate RBI pays banks for parking surplus. (2) MSF (Marginal Standing Facility) — emergency overnight at repo + 25bps. (3) CRR (Cash Reserve Ratio) — % deposits banks must keep with RBI as cash; currently 4.5%; NO interest. (4) SLR (Statutory Liquidity Ratio) — % deposits in Gsecs + gold + cash; currently 18%; earns interest. (5) LAF (Liquidity Adjustment Facility). RBI's CPI INFLATION TARGET: 4% ± 2% (i.e., 2-6%) — statutory since 2016.

questions.stem: In 1969 the Indian Government NATIONALISED how many commercial banks?

options.option_text: 14 BANKS on 19 July 1969 by PM Indira Gandhi (banks with deposit > ₹50 crore)

questions.explanation: 1969 BANK NATIONALISATION — defining moment in Indian economic history. DATE: 19 JULY 1969 ('Bank Nationalisation Day'). PM INDIRA GANDHI used an OVERNIGHT ordinance to nationalise 14 PRIVATE commercial banks with deposits > ₹50 crore, bringing 40% of commercial banking under direct govt control. BANKS NATIONALISED: Central Bank of India, Bank of India, Punjab National Bank, Bank of Baroda, UCO Bank, Canara Bank, United Bank of India, Dena Bank, Syndicate Bank, Union Bank of India, Allahabad Bank, Indian Bank, Indian Overseas Bank, Bank of Maharashtra. LEGAL CHALLENGE: R.C. COOPER v. UNION OF INDIA (1970) — SC struck down the ordinance 10-1 on compensation grounds; Parliament re-enacted as a law with adequate compensation — upheld. SECOND ROUND (1980): 6 more banks nationalised (deposits > ₹200 crore) — Andhra, Corporation, New Bank of India, Oriental Bank of Commerce, Punjab + Sind, Vijaya. Since 2017-2020 merger wave: ~12 PSBs today; 21 private; 43 foreign; 12 small finance; 6 payments banks.

questions.stem: UPI, India's instant mobile payment system launched in 2016, is operated by:

options.option_text: NPCI — National Payments Corporation of India (umbrella organisation for retail payments)

questions.explanation: UPI (UNIFIED PAYMENTS INTERFACE) — INSTANT, 24/7, real-time inter-bank mobile payment system. LAUNCHED: 11 April 2016 by then RBI Governor RAGHURAM RAJAN. OPERATOR: NATIONAL PAYMENTS CORPORATION OF INDIA (NPCI) — a not-for-profit Sec-8 company set up 2008 under RBI + IBA (Indian Banks' Association). FEATURES: (1) single mobile app accesses multiple bank accounts; (2) VPA like name@bank — no need to share bank details; (3) instant transfer 24/7; (4) 2FA. 2024 stats: ~12 BILLION transactions/MONTH; ₹20 lakh crore monthly value; UPI accounts for ~50% of real-time global retail payments. MAJOR UPI apps: PhonePe, Google Pay, Paytm, BHIM, WhatsApp Pay, Amazon Pay, Cred. OTHER NPCI products: IMPS (2010), RuPay (2012 card network), NACH, BBPS, AePS (Aadhaar-enabled Payment System), FASTag (NETC), CTS. UPI has gone GLOBAL: linked with Singapore's PayNow, UAE, Mauritius, Bhutan, Nepal, France, Sri Lanka.

questions.stem: The SARFAESI Act (2002) empowers banks to:

options.option_text: Recover NPAs by SEIZING + SELLING secured assets of defaulters WITHOUT court intervention (for secured loans > ₹1 lakh)

questions.explanation: SARFAESI ACT 2002 — SECURITISATION + RECONSTRUCTION of FINANCIAL ASSETS + ENFORCEMENT of SECURITY INTEREST ACT. Based on Narasimham-II (1998) + Andhyarujina Committee (1999). POWERS: (1) banks can issue 60-DAY NOTICE to defaulter; then take POSSESSION of the pledged asset + auction; NO court intervention needed. (2) creation of ASSET RECONSTRUCTION COMPANIES (ARCs) to purchase stressed loans. Minimum loan: ₹1 lakh. EXCLUSIONS: agri land, amounts <20% of loan. APPEAL: DRT → DRAT → HC (must deposit 50% before appealing). PRE-SARFAESI, banks had to file civil suits taking 10-15 years. NPA (Non-Performing Asset) — loan where interest/principal remains unpaid >90 days. Gross NPA ratio fell from ~11% (2018) to ~3% (2024) through IBC + SARFAESI + govt recapitalisation + AQR. Complementary law: IBC (Insolvency + Bankruptcy Code, 2016) — covers corporate insolvency via NCLT.

questions.stem: PRADHAN MANTRI JAN DHAN YOJANA (PMJDY), launched 28 August 2014, aims at:

options.option_text: UNIVERSAL FINANCIAL INCLUSION — zero-balance account + RuPay card + ₹2L accident cover + overdraft facility for every household

questions.explanation: PMJDY — 'NATIONAL MISSION for FINANCIAL INCLUSION'. LAUNCHED: 28 AUGUST 2014 by PM Narendra Modi; Guinness Record — 1.8 crore accounts in one week. FEATURES: (1) ZERO balance savings a/c (BSBDA); (2) RuPay debit card with ₹1-2L accident insurance; (3) ₹30,000 life cover (2014-15 enrollees); (4) ₹10,000 overdraft facility after 6 months; (5) no minimum balance; (6) free Aadhaar seeding. PROGRESS (Nov 2024): ~53 CRORE accounts; ₹2.33 lakh crore total deposits; 36 crore RuPay cards; 55% female account-holders; 67% rural/semi-urban. IMPACT: backbone of DBT — LPG (PAHAL), PM-KISAN, MGNREGA wages, COVID relief. JAM TRINITY = Jan Dhan + Aadhaar + Mobile = foundational architecture of India's DPI. Today ~95% Indian adults have bank account (World Bank Findex 2021, up from 35% in 2011). Related schemes: PMJJBY (life, ₹2L at ₹436/yr), PMSBY (accident, ₹2L at ₹20/yr), APY (pension, max ₹5000/month after 60 yr age).

questions.stem: CRR (Cash Reserve Ratio) differs from SLR (Statutory Liquidity Ratio) in that:

options.option_text: CRR is kept with RBI in CASH (no interest); SLR is kept BY THE BANK ITSELF in Gsecs + gold + cash (earns interest)
SLR is for only private banks

questions.explanation: CRR — Cash Reserve Ratio (Sec 42 of RBI Act 1934) — % of a bank's NDTL (net demand + time liabilities) to be kept WITH RBI IN CASH, earning NO INTEREST. Current: 4.5%. SLR — Statutory Liquidity Ratio (Sec 24 of Banking Regulation Act 1949) — % of NDTL kept by the bank itself in Gsecs + SDLs + gold + cash. EARNS INTEREST. Current: 18%. PURPOSE: liquidity buffer + force banks to hold safe assets. Historical peaks: CRR 15% (1992); SLR 38.5% (1991). MNEMONIC: CRR = Cash with RBI; SLR = Securities within bank. Other key ratios: LCR (Liquidity Coverage, Basel III) 100%; NSFR 100%; CAR (Capital Adequacy) ≥ 9% (+ Capital Conservation Buffer); PSL (Priority Sector Lending) 40% of net bank credit (agriculture, MSME, housing, education, weaker sections).

questions.stem: NABARD, India's apex rural + agricultural development bank, was established in:

options.option_text: 12 July 1982, on the recommendation of the SIVARAMAN (CRAFICARD) Committee

questions.explanation: NABARD — NATIONAL BANK FOR AGRICULTURE AND RURAL DEVELOPMENT. Established 12 JULY 1982 by the NABARD Act 1981, on recommendations of the CRAFICARD Committee (chaired by B. SIVARAMAN). HQ: Mumbai. Owner: 100% GoI (since 2018). REPLACED: ARDC + ACD of RBI + RPCC. Current Chairman: Shaji K.V. FUNCTIONS: (1) REFINANCE to cooperative banks, RRBs, commercial banks, NBFCs for ag term loans. (2) DIRECT FINANCE to large rural infrastructure projects. (3) RIDF (Rural Infrastructure Development Fund, 1995) — funds state projects; funded by PSB priority-sector shortfalls. (4) Supervision of state + district cooperative banks + RRBs. (5) SHG-Bank Linkage Programme (1992) — ~1.5 crore SHGs — world's largest microfinance programme. (6) Kisan Credit Card scheme. Rural banking structure: (a) RRBs (est. 1975 per Narasimham Committee I); (b) Cooperative banks (3-tier: PACS → DCCB → StCB); (c) SFBs (Small Finance Banks 2015 — AU, Equitas, Ujjivan, Suryoday, etc.).

questions.stem: The NARASIMHAM COMMITTEES (1991 + 1998) are associated with reforms in:

options.option_text: Banking / financial sector — CAR, NPA norms, deregulation of rates, bank consolidation, entry of private banks

questions.explanation: NARASIMHAM COMMITTEES — chaired by M. NARASIMHAM (former RBI Governor, 1977). (1) NARASIMHAM-I (1991) — post 1991 BoP crisis + LPG reforms. REC: (a) reduce SLR 38.5→25% + CRR progressively; (b) DEREGULATE interest rates; (c) allow FOREIGN + NEW PRIVATE banks (led to ICICI, HDFC, Axis, IndusInd entry 1993-94); (d) adopt CAPITAL ADEQUACY NORMS (Basel 8%); (e) introduce ASSET CLASSIFICATION + income recognition (NPAs); (f) structure supervision under Board for Financial Supervision (BFS, RBI). (2) NARASIMHAM-II (1998) — deeper reforms. REC: (a) raise CAR from 8 to 9% (now Basel III+); (b) reduce PSB govt shareholding to 33%; (c) bank MERGERS (seed for 2017-20 merger wave); (d) creation of ASSET RECONSTRUCTION COMPANIES (led to SARFAESI 2002); (e) tech modernisation. Other banking committees: HILTON YOUNG (1926) → RBI Act; CHAKRAVARTY (1985); KHAN (1997); TARAPORE (1997, 2006); RAGHURAM RAJAN (2008) → financial sector reforms; MOR Committee (2014) → financial inclusion.
